title: Bakery Tray Gaps
story: A bakery's display tray is one long row of slots. Each slot holds a pastry, written as its product number, or is empty, written as 0. As customers buy things during the morning, gaps open up all over the tray.

Before the lunch rush, the baker slides every pastry toward the front of the tray so the gaps collect at the back, where the new batch will go. The pastries must stay in the same order as before, because the labels on the glass follow that order.
task: Write compactTray(tray). Rearrange tray in place so all non-zero numbers come first, in their original order, followed by all the zeros. Return nothing.
Do not create a second list. The length of tray stays the same.

examples.explanation: The pastries are 41, 7, 12, in that order. They move to the front and keep that order. The two gaps end up at the back.
9 and 3 are already in place. Only 5 has to move forward, past the two gaps. Sorting would give a different, wrong answer: the order 9, 3, 5 must be kept.

hints: In [0, 41, 0, 7, 12], which slot should 41 end up in? Which slot should 7 end up in? Can you tell just by counting pastries you have already seen?
The k-th pastry you meet from the left always ends up in slot k-1. So as you scan, you always know the next slot that should receive a pastry.
Use two indexes. One scans every slot. The other points at the next slot to fill with a pastry. It moves only when a pastry is placed.

Scan with r, and keep w = next slot to fill, starting at 0. When tray[r] is not 0, swap tray[w] and tray[r], then add 1 to w. The swap carries a gap backwards at the same time as it moves the pastry forwards.
bruteForce: Each time you find a gap, delete it from the list and add a 0 at the end. Or, scan for the first gap and shift everything after it one place left, again and again.

Both are correct, but each delete or shift moves every later slot. A tray of 10,000 slots that is half gaps does about 5,000 shifts of up to 10,000 slots each: tens of millions of moves. Each pastry only needs to move once, straight to its final slot.

js: * @param {number[]} tray  0 means an empty slot; change it in place

tests.note: no gaps, order must not change
defeats swapping each gap with the last slot

js: let w = 0; // next slot that should get a pastry
py: w = 0  # next slot that should get a pastry
walkthrough: The first pastry you meet goes to slot 0, the second to slot 1, and so on. So keep a write index w for the next slot that should hold a pastry, and scan every slot with a read index r.
• r = 0 is a gap. Do nothing. w stays 0.
Everything between w and r is always a gap, so each swap moves a pastry forward and a gap backward. Pastries are placed in the order they are met, which keeps their order.
solution.timeWhy: One pass, with at most one swap per slot.
solution.spaceWhy: Two indexes. The tray is rearranged in place.
solution.takeaway: A read pointer and a write pointer partition a list in place while keeping order: everything before the write pointer is kept, everything between the two pointers is what you are pushing out of the way.
